mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% consistently predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces discount rates and supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger immediate equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors price in recession risks.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a severe weakening in consumer and business demand, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as equity valuations adjust to lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In early recession regimes (defined by declining industrial production and rising unemployment), a drop in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as the market prices in prolonged economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100 and in early recession regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 4.0% indicates persistent inflationary pressures that trigger a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate further monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) indicate a deteriorating labor market under monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors price in recession risks.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS declines and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate exceeding 2.0% signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as equity valuations adjust to stronger fundamentals.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level below 1,300,000 units (HOUST < 1300.0) indicates a contraction in the housing market that triggers negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the broader economy and consumer confidence are impacted.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 1300.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
